genxml.title: Origin 3000 R-brick router registers outside the census (vector space)
genxml.from: shipped kernel and firmware readings; names from the public Linux SN1 router header
genxml.doc: Router register fields and link addresses that the shipped firmware and kernel use, and that the census of the router's vector accesses does not give. Every item here is a software expectation read from shipped code or a public header, not a hardware measurement. The register space is named apart from the census so that offsets which the census already names (the status word, the protection configuration) are not claimed twice.

struct.name: STATUS
struct.from: shipped kernel and firmware readings; names from the public Linux SN1 router header
struct.doc: Status word. The kernel refuses a chip whose part field is not the router part, reads the revision from the top nibble, and treats a port as active when its link-working bit is set. Each link has a two-bit state. The census names the same word as the status and revision register.

struct.name: PROT_CONF
struct.from: shipped kernel and firmware readings; names from the public Linux SN1 router header
struct.doc: Protection configuration. Each low bit lets a reset arriving on that link through. The census gives the access and offset of the same word; the field names come from the public header. Reset value unknown.

struct.name: POSITION
struct.from: shipped kernel and firmware readings; names from the public Linux SN1 router header
struct.doc: Position word that discovery reads to classify a router. A clear bit marks a metarouter or a repeat router. The census does not name this offset.

struct.name: SCRATCH3
struct.from: shipped kernel and firmware readings; names from the public Linux SN1 router header
struct.doc: Scratch register 3. Bit 0 is the router lock: writing 0 releases it. The header names this word as the scratch register itself.

struct.name: SCRATCH3_SETZERO
struct.from: shipped kernel and firmware readings; names from the public Linux SN1 router header
struct.doc: Set-if-zero alias of scratch register 3. A read returns the old lock bit and sets it, so the firmware takes the lock by reading it until the read returns 0.

struct.name: ERROR_LINK1
struct.from: shipped kernel and firmware readings; names from the public Linux SN1 router header
struct.doc: Error status of link 1. The layout is the one the public header gives and the firmware's error decoder prints. The order of the three low flags is not given.

struct.name: RESET_MASK_LINK1
struct.from: shipped kernel and firmware readings; names from the public Linux SN1 router header
struct.doc: Reset mask of link 1. Bit n-1 names a link n. The direction in which the mask applies is inferred, not established.

struct.name: ERROR_LINK2

struct.doc: Error status of link 2. Same layout as link 1.

struct.doc: Reset mask of link 8. Same layout as link 1. The eight mask addresses are not linear: links come in pairs 64 KiB apart, with the second link of a pair 0x800 above the first.
